reasoning: Recent general-election polling for Michigan’s 2026 Senate race is mixed but centers on a very close contest between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers, with several polls showing Rogers narrowly ahead and one late poll showing El-Sayed up by mid-single digits. Taken together, the last 45 days of data point to roughly an R+2 environment in the current Senate race, in a structurally D+2 state by PVI, implying a genuine but modest Republican edge in this particular contest. There is no recent, Michigan-specific presidential general-election polling in the results provided, so the current observable margin applies to the Senate race only.

sources.name: Newsweek summary of EPIC-MRA Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: EPIC-MRA poll of 600 likely Michigan general-election voters found Mike Rogers leading Abdul El-Sayed 46% to 43% in the U.S. Senate race.

sources.name: Breitbart report on Glengariff Group Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Glengariff Group survey, cited in multiple outlets, found Mike Rogers leading Abdul El-Sayed by roughly 10 points in a hypothetical Michigan Senate general-election matchup.

sources.name: WJR coverage of Glengariff Group Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Michigan radio outlet WJR summarizes Glengariff Group findings showing Mike Rogers leading Abdul El-Sayed 49.0% to 38.7% in the Senate race.

sources.name: Michigan News Source summary of Mitchell Research Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Mitchell Research & Communications poll of 406 likely Michigan voters found the Rogers–El-Sayed Senate matchup tied at 45%-45%.

sources.name: Newsweek summary of Mitchell Research Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Mitchell Research poll reported by Newsweek shows a tied general-election race between Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed, 45%-45%, in the Michigan Senate contest.

sources.name: The Hill report on Susquehanna Polling & Research Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Susquehanna Polling & Research survey reported by The Hill finds Abdul El-Sayed leading Mike Rogers 46% to 39% among likely voters in the Michigan Senate race.

sources.name: The Hill summary of EPIC-MRA Michigan Senate polling including Stevens–Rogers matchup
sources.details: EPIC-MRA poll, as described by The Hill, shows Haley Stevens slightly ahead of Mike Rogers in favorability/ballot test terms (44% vs. 42%), suggesting a near-tossup against a more moderate Democrat.

sources.name: Jewish Insider coverage of Michigan Senate general-election polling
sources.details: Jewish Insider highlights a poll showing Haley Stevens leading Mike Rogers by 2 points (47% to 45%) while Abdul El-Sayed trails Rogers 48% to 41% in prospective Michigan Senate general-election matchups.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling Michigan 2026 Democratic Senate primary poll
sources.details: Emerson College Polling survey focuses on the Democratic Senate primary, finding Abdul El-Sayed with a double-digit lead over Haley Stevens, indicating El-Sayed as the likely Democratic nominee.

sources.name: New York Times summary of Michigan Democratic Senate primary polls
sources.details: New York Times polling roundup lists multiple Democratic primary polls (Zenith Research, SoCal Strategies, Emerson, Tavern, Tulchin) all showing Abdul El-Sayed leading Haley Stevens by 10–19 points.

sources.name: MLive report on Tavern Research Michigan Democratic Senate primary poll
sources.details: Tavern Research poll described by MLive finds El-Sayed ahead of Stevens 46%–36% among likely Democratic primary voters.

sources.name: Newsweek roundup of final Michigan Democratic Senate primary polls
sources.details: Newsweek’s synthesis of final Michigan Democratic Senate primary polls cites Mitchell, Zenith, and Emerson, all showing El-Sayed with mid-teen leads over Stevens.

sources.name: Detroit Free Press discussion of RealClearPolitics Michigan Democratic Senate primary average
sources.details: Detroit Free Press article notes a RealClearPolitics polling average putting El-Sayed ahead of Stevens roughly 50.2% to 40.8% in the Democratic Senate primary.

sources.details: Politically.com poll explorer lists multiple Michigan 2026 statewide polls (e.g., for Jocelyn Benson and John James) that are not directly about the U.S. Senate or presidential general-election contests but provide broader electoral context.
